name: Igdaliah
overview: Igdaliah is a male figure described as the man of God and is identified as the father of Hanan. The biblical text does not specify his tribe or further personal details beyond these attributes. His designation highlights a spiritual role or recognition within the biblical narrative.
namesAndTitles: The name Igdaliah means 'y-h-v-h is great,' reflecting a theophoric element that honors the greatness of the Lord. Additionally, he is given the title 'man of God,' which underscores his spiritual standing or connection to divine matters as noted in Jeremiah 35:4.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Igdaliah as the father of Hanan, establishing a direct familial link. Beyond this, no further family relationships are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Igdaliah's significance lies primarily in his identification as a man of God and as the father of Hanan, situating him within the prophetic context of Jeremiah. His mention serves to anchor Hanan's identity and possibly his spiritual heritage, emphasizing the continuity of faithfulness in a challenging period for Israel.
